newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads flat, TCI ekes out gains.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads flat, TCI ekes out gains.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were unchanged to Treasuries on Thursday in one of the quieter days in recent weeks, dealers said, while TCI Communications debt edged higher after earnings were reported as expected.

High-yield telecom bonds outperformed in that market, meanwhile, based on anticipation of further advantageous consolidation for international concerns TeleWest Communications and Comcast UK Cable, traders said.
In the investment grade market, prices rose with Treasuries in the broad market following news that underpinned low inflation and moderate economic growth, players said.
Activity was light with no real spread deterioration seen for the billions of fresh supply to hit the market in the past few days, traders said.

"Usually you would see dealers starting to close their books but we haven't seen that this year," one trader said, adding that generally light Street positions should protect spreads at current levels.

In company specific trade, TCI Communications TCIC.O debt was slightly tighter after the company posted a third quarter net loss of $75 million versus a $26 million loss in Q3 1995. TCI is a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
"The earnings were pretty much as expected and the markets didn't see any great strength either way," a trader said, underscoring that trade was thin.
TCI 7-7/8s of 2026 were quoted at 247 bid, 242 offer near the close compared with a 250 bid, 245 offer late Wednesday.

Turning to high-yielders, prices in for telecom sector bonds outperformed the broad marketplace, led by British concerns TeleWest and Comcast UK, traders said. Most international names were up 1/4 to 1/2 point.
Street talk of a possible merger between Comcast and TeleWest sparked the activity, several traders confirmed.
Comcast UK cable operation's debt traded up two points from 67 to 69 near the close, while TeleWest debt was quoted up about 1/2 point at 67 bid, 67-1/2 offer.

By contrast, domestic provider CAI Wireless traded down at 12-1/4s of 2002 traded down to 92, one trader said. The bonds had been quoted lower prior to Thursday's session, he said, but trades lower than 96 had yet to be spotted.
The downtrade stemmed from growing uncertainty surrounding CAI's alliance with BellAtlantic and NYNEX, a trader said.
"The negotiations are being dragged out and the timing for implementation of their program is cloudy," the trader said.
In other high-yield activity, traders said Trump Castle bonds were up about two points in anticipation of an expected overhaul to Atlantic City's Trump Castle into a Hard Rock Casino Hotel.
Sources said Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc and Britain's Rank Organisation Plc on Tuesday will unveil plans that include a $50 million investment by Rank.
In light issuance, Kaufman & Broad Home Corp issued $125 million Ba3/B-plus rated 10-year senior subordinated notes as 9-5/8s to yield 9.70 percent or 355 basis points over Treasuries.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc is sole manager on the deal.

Investment grade PSI Energy issued $100 million Baa1/BBB-plus rated 10-year debentures with a four-year put option at par to yield 6.35 percent, or 35 basis points over the when-issued five year T-note.
Salomon Brothers is lead manager on the deal.
In the Treasury market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 13/32 to 101-1/32 to yield 6.42 percent. The 10-year note was up 11/32 to 102-18/32 to yield 6.15 percent.
